10 useful gifts for a flight-instructor candidate

Someone preparing to teach flying may value tools for explaining, organizing and presenting ideas. This guide focuses on gifts that support their own preparation style. It does not assume that more equipment or another course will make them a better instructor.

By Pilot Gift Guide · From the team behind ATC · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEHow to chooseThe listRelated guides

How to choose

Find out how the candidate practices teaching: paper, whiteboard, tablet or a mixture. Choose materials that fit that routine. Keep technical references and courses aligned with the program they are following, and let the candidate decide what belongs in their teaching kit.

The list

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    A portable whiteboard

    Choose a size they can store and carry. Include suitable markers and a cloth rather than a bulky stand.

  2. 2

    A tabletop model airplane

    A simple model can help illustrate ideas during practice explanations. Choose durability and clear shape over collectible detail.

  3. 3

    A document camera contribution

    Useful only if they want to demonstrate paper or small objects remotely. Confirm the computer connection and available desk space.

  4. 4

    A presentation notebook

    Choose a format for outlines and teaching practice notes. Leave room for the candidate’s own organization and revisions.

  5. 5

    A timer for practice lessons

    A quiet, easy-to-read timer can support rehearsal. Avoid presenting a particular timing method as a required teaching technique.

  6. 6

    A book stand

    Make reference material easier to consult while speaking or writing. Check the size of the books it needs to support.

  7. 7

    The reference book they requested

    Match the edition and format exactly. A current course list is more useful than a generic bestseller ranking.

  8. 8

    A teaching-materials pouch

    Keep markers, cards and small props together. Choose a pouch that fits their existing bag rather than creating another bag to carry.

  9. 9

    A rehearsal audience

    Offer to listen to an explanation and give feedback they ask for. Your attention can be the gift without pretending to assess technical competence.

  10. 10

    A celebration after the preparation period

    Choose something personal and flexible, such as a favorite meal together. Recognize the effort regardless of whether the schedule changes.

These are editorial recommendations and planning ideas, not hands-on test results. Read our selection approach and ATC disclosure.
